title: NY S08828: Implements transparency requirements for developers of AI models; requires the establishment of an office for oversite of AI model developer transparency and reporting; makes related provisions.

obligations: A large frontier developer shall write, implement, comply with, and clearly and conspicuously publish on its internet website a frontier AI framework covering specified topics (§ 1421 subd. 1)
A large frontier developer shall review and update its frontier AI framework at least once per year and publish any material modification with justification within thirty days (§ 1421 subd. 2)
Before or concurrently with deploying a new or substantially modified frontier model, a frontier developer shall publish a transparency report containing specified information (§ 1421 subd. 3(a))
A large frontier developer shall include in the transparency report summaries of catastrophic risk assessments, results, third party evaluator involvement, and other steps (§ 1421 subd. 3(b))

A frontier developer shall not make a materially false or misleading statement about catastrophic risk or its management; a large frontier developer shall not make a materially false or misleading statement about implementation of or compliance with its frontier AI framework (§ 1421 subd. 4(a))
If a frontier developer redacts information, it shall describe the character and justification of the redaction and retain unredacted information for five years (§ 1421 subd. 5(b))
The office shall establish a mechanism for reporting critical safety incidents (§ 1422 subd. 1)
A large frontier developer shall transmit to the office a summary of any assessment of catastrophic risk from internal use every three months or on another agreed schedule (§ 1422 subd. 2(a))

A frontier developer shall report any critical safety incident to the office within seventy two hours, or within twenty four hours to an appropriate authority if imminent risk of death or serious physical injury (§ 1422 subd. 3)
The office shall review critical safety incident reports and may review reports submitted by members of the public (§ 1422 subd. 4)
The office shall produce an annual report beginning January 1, 2028 with specified information (§ 1422 subd. 7)

A frontier developer that intends to comply with critical safety incident reporting via designated federal standards shall declare its intent to the office and send copies of federal reports concurrently (§ 1422 subd. 9)

A large frontier developer shall file a current disclosure statement with the office and pay the required share before developing, deploying, or operating a frontier model in New York (§ 1428 subd. 1)
A large frontier developer shall renew its disclosure statement every two years, upon transfer of ownership, or upon material change (§ 1428 subd. 2)
A large frontier developer shall include specified identifying and contact information in its disclosure statement (§ 1428 subd. 3)
Large frontier developers shall be assessed pro rata shares to defray operating expenses (§ 1428 subd. 4)
The office shall maintain and publish a list of large frontier developers who have filed disclosure statements, excluding contact information (§ 1428 subd. 6)
The office may adopt rules and regulations to implement the article (§ 1429)
prohibitions: A frontier developer shall not make a materially false or misleading statement about catastrophic risk from its frontier models or its management of catastrophic risk (§ 1421 subd. 4(a)(i))
A large frontier developer shall not make a materially false or misleading statement about its implementation of, or compliance with, its frontier AI framework (§ 1421 subd. 4(a)(ii))

No large frontier developer may develop, deploy, or operate a frontier model in whole or in part in New York state without having a current disclosure statement filed with the office and paying the required share (§ 1428 subd. 1)

Failure by a frontier developer to meet the standards of or comply with requirements stated by a designated federal law, regulation, or guidance document constitutes a violation of this article (§ 1422 subd. 9(b)(ii))
The office shall not include information in its annual report that would compromise trade secrets, cybersecurity, public safety, national security, or violate law (§ 1422 subd. 7(b))

key_definitions: Affiliate: a person controlling, controlled by, or under common control with a specified person, directly or indirectly, through one or more intermediaries (§ 1420 subd. 1)

Artificial intelligence model: an engineered or machine based system that varies in its level of autonomy and that can, for explicit or implicit objectives, infer from the input it receives how to generate outputs that can influence physical or virtual environments (§ 1420 subd. 2)

Catastrophic risk: a foreseeable and material risk that a frontier developer's development, storage, use, or deployment of a frontier model will materially contribute to the death of, or serious injury to, more than fifty people or more than one billion dollars in damage to, or loss of, property arising from a single incident involving a frontier model doing specified acts, with exclusions for publicly accessible information, lawful federal activity, and harm where the model did not materially contribute (§ 1420 subd. 3)

Critical safety incident: unauthorized access to, modification of, or exfiltration of model weights resulting in death or bodily injury; harm from materialization of a catastrophic risk; loss of control causing death or bodily injury; or a frontier model using deceptive techniques against the developer to subvert controls outside an evaluation and demonstrating materially increased catastrophic risk (§ 1420 subd. 4)

Deploy: to make a frontier model available to a third party for use, modification, copying, or combination with other software, excluding making it available for the primary purpose of developing or evaluating the model (§ 1420 subd. 5)
Foundation model: an artificial intelligence model trained on a broad data set, designed for generality of output, and adaptable to a wide range of distinctive tasks (§ 1420 subd. 6)
Frontier AI framework: documented technical and organizational protocols to manage, assess, and mitigate catastrophic risks (§ 1420 subd. 7)

Frontier developer: a person who has trained, or initiated the training of, a frontier model, with respect to which the person has used, or intends to use, at least as much computing power as the technical specifications in subdivision nine (§ 1420 subd. 8)

Frontier model: a foundation model trained using a quantity of computing power greater than 10^26 integer or floating point operations, including original training and subsequent fine tuning, reinforcement learning, or other material modifications (§ 1420 subd. 9)

Large frontier developer: a frontier developer that together with its affiliates collectively had annual gross revenues in excess of five hundred million dollars in the preceding calendar year (§ 1420 subd. 10)
Model weight: a numerical parameter in a frontier model that is adjusted through training and that helps determine how inputs are transformed into outputs (§ 1420 subd. 11)
Department: the department of financial services (§ 1420 subd. 12)
Property: tangible or intangible property (§ 1420 subd. 13)

Person: an individual, proprietorship, firm, partnership, joint venture, syndicate, business trust, company, corporation, limited liability company, association, committee, or any other nongovernmental organization or group of persons acting in concert (§ 1420 subd. 14)
Superintendent: the superintendent of financial services (§ 1420 subd. 15)
Office: an office within the department of financial services, which shall report to the superintendent of financial services and is tasked with implementation of this article (§ 1420 subd. 16)

If a large frontier developer, write, implement, comply with, and publish a frontier AI framework covering all required topics (§ 1421 subd. 1)

Avoid materially false or misleading statements about catastrophic risk and framework compliance (§ 1421 subd. 4)

If a large frontier developer, transmit summaries of internal use catastrophic risk assessments every three months or on an agreed schedule (§ 1422 subd. 2)
If using a designated federal alternative for critical safety incident reporting, declare intent to the office and send copies of federal reports concurrently (§ 1422 subd. 9)
Monitor and comply with any rules and regulations adopted by the office (§ 1429)

The office within the Department of Financial Services (§ 1420 subd. 16)

Publishing required information as part of a larger document such as a system card or model card is deemed compliance (§ 1421 subd. 3(c))
Reports of critical safety incidents and internal use assessments are exempt from disclosure under article six of the public officers law (§ 1422 subd. 6)
A frontier developer may comply with critical safety incident reporting by meeting designated federal standards after declaring intent to the office (§ 1422 subd. 8, 9)
The article does not apply to loss of equity as property damage (§ 1423)
The article applies only to frontier models developed, deployed, or operating in whole or in part in New York state (§ 1425)

What it does

The Responsible AI Safety and Education (RAISE) Act requires developers of large frontier artificial intelligence models to publish a frontier AI framework and transparency reports, report critical safety incidents, and file disclosure statements with the Department of Financial Services. It establishes an office within the department to oversee transparency and reporting, and authorizes civil penalties for violations. The act applies to frontier models developed, deployed, or operating in whole or in part in New York.

Who it applies to

  • Frontier developers, defined as persons who have trained or initiated training of a frontier model with computing power greater than 10^26 operations (§ 1420 subd. 8)
  • Large frontier developers, defined as frontier developers with affiliates collectively having annual gross revenues over $500 million in the preceding calendar year (§ 1420 subd. 10)
  • The office within the Department of Financial Services (§ 1420 subd. 16)
  • The attorney general (§ 1427 subd. 1)

Effective date

January 1, 2027

Key definitions

  • Affiliate: a person controlling, controlled by, or under common control with a specified person, directly or indirectly, through one or more intermediaries (§ 1420 subd. 1)
  • Artificial intelligence model: an engineered or machine based system that varies in its level of autonomy and that can, for explicit or implicit objectives, infer from the input it receives how to generate outputs that can influence physical or virtual environments (§ 1420 subd. 2)
  • Catastrophic risk: a foreseeable and material risk that a frontier developer's development, storage, use, or deployment of a frontier model will materially contribute to the death of, or serious injury to, more than fifty people or more than one billion dollars in damage to, or loss of, property arising from a single incident involving a frontier model doing specified acts, with exclusions for publicly accessible information, lawful federal activity, and harm where the model did not materially contribute (§ 1420 subd. 3)
  • Critical safety incident: unauthorized access to, modification of, or exfiltration of model weights resulting in death or bodily injury; harm from materialization of a catastrophic risk; loss of control causing death or bodily injury; or a frontier model using deceptive techniques against the developer to subvert controls outside an evaluation and demonstrating materially increased catastrophic risk (§ 1420 subd. 4)
  • Deploy: to make a frontier model available to a third party for use, modification, copying, or combination with other software, excluding making it available for the primary purpose of developing or evaluating the model (§ 1420 subd. 5)
  • Foundation model: an artificial intelligence model trained on a broad data set, designed for generality of output, and adaptable to a wide range of distinctive tasks (§ 1420 subd. 6)
  • Frontier AI framework: documented technical and organizational protocols to manage, assess, and mitigate catastrophic risks (§ 1420 subd. 7)
  • Frontier developer: a person who has trained, or initiated the training of, a frontier model, with respect to which the person has used, or intends to use, at least as much computing power as the technical specifications in subdivision nine (§ 1420 subd. 8)
  • Frontier model: a foundation model trained using a quantity of computing power greater than 10^26 integer or floating point operations, including original training and subsequent fine tuning, reinforcement learning, or other material modifications (§ 1420 subd. 9)
  • Large frontier developer: a frontier developer that together with its affiliates collectively had annual gross revenues in excess of five hundred million dollars in the preceding calendar year (§ 1420 subd. 10)
  • Model weight: a numerical parameter in a frontier model that is adjusted through training and that helps determine how inputs are transformed into outputs (§ 1420 subd. 11)
  • Department: the department of financial services (§ 1420 subd. 12)
  • Property: tangible or intangible property (§ 1420 subd. 13)
  • Person: an individual, proprietorship, firm, partnership, joint venture, syndicate, business trust, company, corporation, limited liability company, association, committee, or any other nongovernmental organization or group of persons acting in concert (§ 1420 subd. 14)
  • Superintendent: the superintendent of financial services (§ 1420 subd. 15)
  • Office: an office within the department of financial services, which shall report to the superintendent of financial services and is tasked with implementation of this article (§ 1420 subd. 16)

Obligations

  • A large frontier developer shall write, implement, comply with, and clearly and conspicuously publish on its internet website a frontier AI framework covering specified topics (§ 1421 subd. 1)
  • A large frontier developer shall review and update its frontier AI framework at least once per year and publish any material modification with justification within thirty days (§ 1421 subd. 2)
  • Before or concurrently with deploying a new or substantially modified frontier model, a frontier developer shall publish a transparency report containing specified information (§ 1421 subd. 3(a))
  • A large frontier developer shall include in the transparency report summaries of catastrophic risk assessments, results, third party evaluator involvement, and other steps (§ 1421 subd. 3(b))
  • A frontier developer shall not make a materially false or misleading statement about catastrophic risk or its management; a large frontier developer shall not make a materially false or misleading statement about implementation of or compliance with its frontier AI framework (§ 1421 subd. 4(a))
  • If a frontier developer redacts information, it shall describe the character and justification of the redaction and retain unredacted information for five years (§ 1421 subd. 5(b))
  • The office shall establish a mechanism for reporting critical safety incidents (§ 1422 subd. 1)
  • A large frontier developer shall transmit to the office a summary of any assessment of catastrophic risk from internal use every three months or on another agreed schedule (§ 1422 subd. 2(a))
  • A frontier developer shall report any critical safety incident to the office within seventy two hours, or within twenty four hours to an appropriate authority if imminent risk of death or serious physical injury (§ 1422 subd. 3)
  • The office shall review critical safety incident reports and may review reports submitted by members of the public (§ 1422 subd. 4)
  • The office shall produce an annual report beginning January 1, 2028 with specified information (§ 1422 subd. 7)
  • A frontier developer that intends to comply with critical safety incident reporting via designated federal standards shall declare its intent to the office and send copies of federal reports concurrently (§ 1422 subd. 9)
  • A large frontier developer shall file a current disclosure statement with the office and pay the required share before developing, deploying, or operating a frontier model in New York (§ 1428 subd. 1)
  • A large frontier developer shall renew its disclosure statement every two years, upon transfer of ownership, or upon material change (§ 1428 subd. 2)
  • A large frontier developer shall include specified identifying and contact information in its disclosure statement (§ 1428 subd. 3)
  • Large frontier developers shall be assessed pro rata shares to defray operating expenses (§ 1428 subd. 4)
  • The office shall maintain and publish a list of large frontier developers who have filed disclosure statements, excluding contact information (§ 1428 subd. 6)
  • The office may adopt rules and regulations to implement the article (§ 1429)

Prohibitions

  • A frontier developer shall not make a materially false or misleading statement about catastrophic risk from its frontier models or its management of catastrophic risk (§ 1421 subd. 4(a)(i))
  • A large frontier developer shall not make a materially false or misleading statement about its implementation of, or compliance with, its frontier AI framework (§ 1421 subd. 4(a)(ii))
  • No large frontier developer may develop, deploy, or operate a frontier model in whole or in part in New York state without having a current disclosure statement filed with the office and paying the required share (§ 1428 subd. 1)
  • Failure by a frontier developer to meet the standards of or comply with requirements stated by a designated federal law, regulation, or guidance document constitutes a violation of this article (§ 1422 subd. 9(b)(ii))
  • The office shall not include information in its annual report that would compromise trade secrets, cybersecurity, public safety, national security, or violate law (§ 1422 subd. 7(b))

Penalties and enforcement

The attorney general may bring a civil action to recover a civil penalty up to $1 million for a first violation and up to $3 million per subsequent violation, determined based on severity, for specified failures by a large frontier developer (§ 1427 subd. 1). The office may levy civil penalties of $1,000 per day for failure to file a disclosure or correct false information, plus an amount equal to assessments owed (§ 1428 subd. 5). No private right of action is created (§ 1427 subd. 2). The office enforces disclosure and assessment requirements; the attorney general enforces other violations.

How it affects AI deployment

  • A large frontier developer must publish a frontier AI framework and keep it current before deploying frontier models in New York (§ 1421 subd. 1, 2)
  • Before or concurrently with deploying a new or substantially modified frontier model, a frontier developer must publish a transparency report; a large frontier developer must include catastrophic risk assessment summaries (§ 1421 subd. 3)
  • A large frontier developer must file a current disclosure statement and pay pro rata assessments before developing, deploying, or operating a frontier model in New York (§ 1428 subd. 1, 4)
  • A frontier developer must report critical safety incidents to the office within 72 hours, or within 24 hours to appropriate authorities if imminent risk of death or serious physical injury (§ 1422 subd. 3)
  • A large frontier developer must transmit summaries of internal use catastrophic risk assessments every three months or on an agreed schedule (§ 1422 subd. 2)
  • Violations can result in civil penalties up to $1 million for a first violation and $3 million per subsequent violation, plus $1,000 per day for disclosure failures (§ 1427 subd. 1; § 1428 subd. 5)
  • The act does not create a private right of action, so enforcement is by the attorney general or the office (§ 1427 subd. 2)
  • The act applies only to frontier models developed, deployed, or operating in whole or in part in New York (§ 1425)
  • Accredited colleges and universities and the Empire AI consortium are exempt when engaging in academic research or as defined (§ 1426)
  • Loss of equity does not count as property damage for purposes of the article (§ 1423)

Notable exemptions

  • Accredited colleges and universities in New York state, to the extent engaging in academic research regarding artificial intelligence models (§ 1426 subd. 1)
  • The Empire AI consortium or the institute as defined by section 361 of the economic development law (§ 1426 subd. 2)
  • A frontier developer may redact published documents to protect trade secrets, cybersecurity, public safety, national security, or to comply with law, but must describe redactions and retain unredacted information for five years (§ 1421 subd. 5)
  • A statement made in good faith and reasonable under the circumstances is not a violation of the false statement prohibition (§ 1421 subd. 4(b))
  • Publishing required information as part of a larger document such as a system card or model card is deemed compliance (§ 1421 subd. 3(c))
  • Reports of critical safety incidents and internal use assessments are exempt from disclosure under article six of the public officers law (§ 1422 subd. 6)
  • A frontier developer may comply with critical safety incident reporting by meeting designated federal standards after declaring intent to the office (§ 1422 subd. 8, 9)
  • The article does not apply to loss of equity as property damage (§ 1423)
  • The article applies only to frontier models developed, deployed, or operating in whole or in part in New York state (§ 1425)

Compliance steps

  • Determine whether you are a frontier developer or large frontier developer under the definitions in § 1420, including computing power and revenue thresholds
  • If a large frontier developer, write, implement, comply with, and publish a frontier AI framework covering all required topics (§ 1421 subd. 1)
  • Review and update the frontier AI framework at least annually and publish any material modification with justification within thirty days (§ 1421 subd. 2)
  • Before or concurrently with deploying a new or substantially modified frontier model, publish a transparency report with required information; if a large frontier developer, include catastrophic risk assessment summaries (§ 1421 subd. 3)
  • Avoid materially false or misleading statements about catastrophic risk and framework compliance (§ 1421 subd. 4)
  • If redacting published documents, describe the redactions and retain unredacted information for five years (§ 1421 subd. 5)
  • File a current disclosure statement with the office and pay the pro rata assessment before developing, deploying, or operating a frontier model in New York; renew every two years or upon transfer or material change (§ 1428 subd. 1, 2, 3, 4)
  • Report critical safety incidents to the office within 72 hours, or within 24 hours to appropriate authorities if imminent risk of death or serious physical injury (§ 1422 subd. 3)
  • If a large frontier developer, transmit summaries of internal use catastrophic risk assessments every three months or on an agreed schedule (§ 1422 subd. 2)
  • If using a designated federal alternative for critical safety incident reporting, declare intent to the office and send copies of federal reports concurrently (§ 1422 subd. 9)
  • Monitor and comply with any rules and regulations adopted by the office (§ 1429)
